lines: +// Package audit implements Rancher's audit log: an access-log style HTTP
+// middleware that writes one entry per request after the handler returns.
+// The middleware is registered on Rancher.Auth in pkg/rancher/rancher.go:
+// When audit logging is disabled, a passthrough middleware is used instead.
+// steve's Middleware.Chain composes as m(middleware(next)), so the
+// authenticator runs first and the audit middleware wraps Rancher.Handler.
+// The audit middleware must remain after the authenticator and outside
+// Rancher.Handler. It captures the request user once, before downstream
+// handlers can change it, and must observe the final response and mutations
+// to the audit [User]. Moving it into Rancher.Handler or a per-route chain
+// can change the captured identity or leave routes unaudited.
+//  1. The authenticator sets the request user, including error and
+//     unauthenticated identities when authentication fails or is absent.
+//  2. The audit middleware creates a [User] from that context, stores it
+//     for downstream mutation via [FromContext], and wraps the request
+//     body and response writer as needed.
+//  3. Rancher.Handler and its downstream middleware handle the request.
+//  4. After the handler returns, the audit middleware builds the entry from
+//     the final [User] and response, then writes it.
+// Every request reaching Rancher.Handler passes through the audit middleware,
+// including public login routes and SCIM. No entry is written when:
+//   - the resolved policy and verbosity exclude the request URI; or
+//   - the response writer is hijacked, as for websockets and tunnels.
+// The [User] is a shared pointer created before the handler runs. Downstream
+// middleware may change it, and the final entry reflects those changes.
+// Model: Name, Identity and Group describe the effective identity, meaning who
+// the request is authorized as. ImpersonatedBy describes the real authenticated
+// caller and is set only when a user impersonation succeeded. Extra is captured
+// when the entry is created and is not refreshed, see the compatibility rule
+// below. RequestUser and RequestGroups hold the raw Impersonate-* headers,
+// and are recorded before authorization, so a denied impersonation still
+// shows the attempted target while the identity stays the real caller.
+// The identity changes in three ways, and each has one owner:
+//   - Authentication substitution: the service-account and token-review
+//     authenticators replace the error user. There is no real caller, so only
+//     the effective identity changes. requests.NewAuthenticatedFilter applies
+//   - User impersonation: the impersonation filter replaces the request user
+//     and calls [User.Impersonate] with the user before and after the swap.
+//   - SCIM: the SCIM token authenticator sets the identity of the SCIM caller
+// Preserve these invariants when changing the [User]:
+//   - Change the identity only through [User.SetIdentity] and
+//     [User.Impersonate], so Name, Identity, Group and ImpersonatedBy cannot
+//   - Do not change the content or format of existing fields for requests that
+//     are not affected by a bug. Log consumers parse them. New information
+//     goes in new optional fields that are omitted when empty, as Identity and
+//   - Group and Extra initially alias memory owned by the request context's
+//     user info. Replace them rather than modifying them in place.
+//   - Name is the stable, unique Rancher user ID, not a human-readable name.
+//     Who the user is, as a person and a provider, goes in Identity.
+//   - ExcludeGroups clears the groups of the user and of ImpersonatedBy on the
+//     shared [User]. This is safe only because it happens after the request has
+// [User].Identity and ImpersonatedBy are opt-in, through [WithIncludeUsername], which Rancher
+// ties to the audit-log-username feature. It is read once when the entry is created. When it is off,
+// nothing is derived or assigned: no identity or impersonator is set and no user lookup is made, so
+// entries keep their previous format for consumers that parse them strictly. The flag is meant to
+// An [Identity] holds the human-readable Username, the Provider ID that authenticated the session
+// and the PrincipalID. A username alone is ambiguous, because the same name can exist on several
+// providers and can change, so it is meant to be read with its provider. Name stays the key for
+// correlation. Each field is optional and the whole Identity is omitted when empty. The same type
+// The Identity of a user is chosen in this order:
+//  1. The authoritative identity the authenticator attached to the request user
+//     with [WithIdentity], read through [IdentityInfo]. It is used as a whole and
+//     is not mixed with the other sources, because that could pair a username
+//     with the wrong provider. It is not part of the user extras, because
+//     extras are forwarded as impersonation headers and checked against the
+//  2. The "username" user extra (see [UsernameFromExtra]). It gives only the
+//     Username, because the extras of a user linked to several providers do not
+//     say which provider a value belongs to.
+//  3. When the entry is written and it is still empty, the user record that the
+//     respective Name refers to: its username, then its display name (see
+//     [UserResolver] and [WithUserResolver]). It gives only the Username.
+//     System identities have no record and keep an empty Identity.
+// The authoritative identity is attached to the request user object itself, so
+// it is lost whenever that object is replaced. After a user impersonation the
+// replacement user has only the extras sent in the Impersonate-Extra-* headers,
+// so the effective Identity usually comes from the lookup and has no provider,
+// and it is never carried over from the real caller. ImpersonatedBy.Identity is
+// read from the caller before the replacement, so it keeps the authoritative
+//   - Do not add fallback usernames to the extras built by the token
+//     authenticator. They are forwarded as impersonation headers, and the
+//     per-user impersonator ClusterRole (pkg/impersonation) only allows the
+//     username values stored in the user's attributes, so an unlisted value is
+//     rejected with "not allowed to impersonate extras".
+//   - No identity source may depend on data that the verbosity level drops
+//     (request or response headers and bodies). The login name from a login
+//     request body is read regardless of level for this reason.
+//   - Authentication providers decide who a user is. The audit package only
+//     reads it. The token authenticator reports the login name, the provider
+//     and the principal ID of the token the session was authenticated with.
+//   - Service-account impersonation is not modeled. The request user is not
+//     replaced there (the downstream token is created for the service account
+//     in the cluster proxy), so Name stays the real caller and ImpersonatedBy
+//     is unset. The meaning of Name therefore depends on the kind of
+//     impersonation. This needs its own design.
+//   - After a user impersonation, Name and Group are the impersonated user's,
+//     but Extra still holds the extras of the authenticated caller, for example
+//     its request token ID. This is kept on purpose, because log consumers
+//     may rely on it. ImpersonatedBy has the caller's name, username and groups,
+//     so the caller does not have to be inferred from Extra. If a use case needs
+//     more of the caller, add it to Impersonator as an additive field.
+//   - Routes that do not run requests.NewAuthenticatedFilter retain the
+//     initially captured identity. Every route that runs the impersonation
+//     filter also runs NewAuthenticatedFilter, but a new route that does not
+//   - Authentication failures are captured as "system:cattle:error" or
+//     "system:unauthenticated". Consumers should treat these as "no identity".
+// UserResolver looks up a Rancher user by ID. It returns the user's username and display name,
+// and false if the user does not exist.
+type UserResolver func(userID string) (username, displayName string, ok bool)
+// Option configures the audit log middleware.
+// WithUserResolver sets the resolver used to fill in the username of audit entries that have none.
+// WithIncludeUsername sets the function that tells whether the entries get the username of the user and
+// of the impersonator. It is called for every entry, so it can follow a feature flag. Without this
+// option the entries do not get them, so that the entry format only grows for those who opted in, as
+// log consumers may parse entries strictly.
auditLogEntry := newLog(verbosityLevel, auditUser, req, wrappedRw, reqTimestamp, respTimestamp, rawReqBody, userName, scim)
+// TestMiddlewareLoginNameIsIndependentOfLevel guards the forced read of login request bodies: the login name
+// comes from the request body, so it must be captured at every level even though the body itself is only
+		"LevelRequest login":         {level: auditlogv1.LevelRequest, uri: "/v3-public/localProviders/local?action=login", wantLoginName: "alice", wantBody: true},
+		"LevelRequestResponse login": {level: auditlogv1.LevelRequestResponse, uri: "/v3-public/localProviders/local?action=login", wantLoginName: "alice", wantBody: true},
+				assert.Equal(t, loginBody, string(body), "handler must still be able to read the body")
// User holds information about the user who caused the audit log
+	// Name is the Rancher user ID (for example "user-h9q7h") for authenticated users, or a
+	// system identity such as "system:unauthenticated". It is not a login name and is opaque
+	// to humans; use Identity to identify a person.
+	// Identity says who the user is in terms of a person and the auth provider that knows them. It
+	// is best-effort and may be omitted. See [Identity].
+	// ImpersonatedBy is the real authenticated caller. It is set only when the caller successfully
+	// impersonated another user, in which case Name, Identity, Group and Extra describe the
+	// impersonated (effective) user. A denied impersonation leaves it unset.
+	// withIdentity is whether Identity and ImpersonatedBy are collected for this entry. It is decided
+	// once when the entry is created, from the audit-log-username feature, so when it is off no
+	// identity is looked up or assigned.
+// Identity describes a user as a person known to an auth provider. The user ID in [User].Name stays
+// the key for correlation: a username is not unique across providers and can change, so it is
+	// Username is the human-readable name of the user, such as the login name.
+	// Provider is the ID of the auth provider that authenticated the session, such as "local" or "github".
+	// PrincipalID is the ID of the provider's principal for the user, such as "github_user://12345".
+// IsZero returns whether the identity holds no information.
+// ref returns a pointer to the identity, or nil when it is empty so that it is omitted from the entry.
+// Impersonator identifies the real authenticated caller of an impersonated request.
+	// Name is the Rancher user ID of the caller, with the same meaning as [User].Name.
+	// Identity is the identity of the caller, with the same meaning as [User].Identity.
+// SetIdentity sets Name, Identity and Group to the effective identity of the request from info.
+// Group is replaced, not modified in place, because it shares memory with info.
+// Extra and ImpersonatedBy are left unchanged. Extra is captured when the entry is created, and
+// only the SCIM authenticator replaces it, so the content of existing entries does not change.
+// SetImpersonatedBy records real as the authenticated caller that impersonated the effective user. It
+// does nothing unless identities are collected for the entry.
+// Impersonate records that real is impersonating effective: effective becomes the identity of the
+// request and real is kept as ImpersonatedBy. Call it where the request user is replaced.
+// clearGroups removes the groups of the user and of the impersonator, for the ExcludeGroups option.
+// UsernameFromExtra returns the human-readable name from the "username" user extra, or "" if there is none.
+// The extra can hold several values, one per linked auth provider, in no meaningful order. The
+// smallest non-empty value is returned so the result is stable across requests.
+// fillIdentity sets the username of an empty Identity, and of an empty ImpersonatedBy.Identity, from
+// the user record that the respective Name refers to: the user's username, otherwise its display
+// name. It runs when the entry is written, so the identities are final. Users without a record, such
+// as system identities, keep an empty Identity.
+// An identity that already has a provider or principal is left alone. The record does not say which
+// provider a name came from, so adding it could attribute a name to the wrong provider.
+// IdentityInfo is implemented by a user.Info that carries an authoritative identity, chosen by the
+// WithIdentity returns info carrying identity as its authoritative identity. It is kept out of the
+// user extras on purpose: extras are forwarded as impersonation headers and checked against the
+// impersonator role. The identity is lost whenever the request user is replaced, for example by
+// impersonation, so it can never describe a different user than the one it was set for. An empty
+// IdentityFromInfo returns the identity for info, which is empty if there is none. The authoritative
+// identity from [WithIdentity] wins as a whole, because mixing it with another source could pair a
+// username with the wrong provider. Otherwise the identity has only the username from the user extras.
// FromContext gets the user information from the given context.
+		{name: "order does not matter", extra: map[string][]string{"username": {"admin", "user@example.com"}}, want: "admin"},
+		{name: "empty values are skipped", extra: map[string][]string{"username": {"", "admin"}}, want: "admin"},
+	assert.Equal(t, &Identity{Username: "admin"}, got.Identity, "extras only give the username, not a provider")
+		{name: "explicit identity wins over extras", info: WithIdentity(base, explicit), want: explicit},
+		{name: "explicit identity without username is not mixed with extras", info: WithIdentity(base, Identity{Provider: "github"}), want: Identity{Provider: "github"}},
+		{name: "empty explicit identity falls back to extras", info: WithIdentity(base, Identity{}), want: Identity{Username: "from-extra"}},
+		{name: "plain info uses only the username extra", info: base, want: Identity{Username: "from-extra"}},
+		{name: "plain info without extras", info: &user.DefaultInfo{Name: "u-2"}, want: Identity{}},
+	assert.Same(t, base, WithIdentity(base, Identity{}), "an empty identity must return the info unchanged")
+	assert.Equal(t, map[string][]string{"username": {"from-extra"}}, got.Extra, "extras must not be changed")
+	type record struct{ username, displayName string }
+		{name: "username from the user record", resolver: resolver, user: User{Name: "u-local", withIdentity: true}, want: &Identity{Username: "admin"}},
+		{name: "display name when the record has no username", resolver: resolver, user: User{Name: "u-external", withIdentity: true}, want: &Identity{Username: "Jane Doe"}},
+		{name: "empty when the record has neither", resolver: resolver, user: User{Name: "u-nameless", withIdentity: true}},
+		{name: "empty when the user does not exist", resolver: resolver, user: User{Name: "system:unauthenticated", withIdentity: true}},
+		{name: "existing identity is kept", resolver: resolver, user: User{Name: "u-local", Identity: provided, withIdentity: true}, want: provided},
+		{name: "empty name is not resolved", resolver: resolver, user: User{withIdentity: true}},
+		{name: "no resolver", resolver: nil, user: User{Name: "u-local", withIdentity: true}},
+		{name: "identities are off", resolver: resolver, user: User{Name: "u-local"}},
+	assert.Equal(t, map[string][]string{"old": {"x"}}, u.Extra, "SetIdentity must not touch Extra")
